data.title: Get your pasta passport  for 'The Taste of Italy'
data.description: The Embassy of Italy in Bangkok, Thailand, invites lovers of Italian cuisine to enjoy their favourite dishes and earn prizes during "Taste of Italy Passport: Discover. Taste. Collect. Unlock", which will take place throughout November.

data.title: Hello Kitty firm apologises, scraps TV tie-up after China anger
data.description: BEIJING - Sanrio, the Japanese company that owns the popular Hello Kitty character, apologised on Thursday over its tie-up with a TV spy drama criticised as anti-China, cancelling a merchandise collaboration with the show.

data.title: Falklands War munitions fashioned into ‘Chalice of Peace’ for the pope
data.description: BUENOS AIRES - Combining the remnants of shell casings and other items from the Falklands War, Argentine silversmith Juan Carlos Pallarols is crafting a "Chalice of Peace" to give to Pope Leo XIV when he visits Argentina next month.

data.title: ‘My blood was spilled here’: Tanzania election violence not forgotten
data.description: DAR ES SALAAM - A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.

data.description: MONTREAL, Quebec - Canada and the European Union will craft “a new chapter” in their alliance at a summit that opens on Thursday, the EU chief said, as they navigate uncertain relations with the United States.

data.title: Indonesia in  focus during 'Sudo Rungu'
data.description: Indonesian contemporary artist Roby Dwi Antono is now showcasing his first solo exhibition in Thailand titled "Sudo Rungu: Echoes Of Fire", which draws on memories from his father who worked as a blacksmith, at Moca Museum of Contemporary Art from now until Jan 3.

data.title: Thai property groups seek mortgage tax relief and property tax changes

data.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles into East Sea
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea fired short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul’s defence ministry said, less than a week after South Korea proposed talks over a growing border row.

data.title: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite ban
data.description: KABUL - Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan more than quadrupled in 2026 despite a Taliban government ban, the United Nations said Thursday, urging that impoverished farmers needed alternatives to the lucrative crop.

data.title: Cuba wins UN vote against US embargo but support dips
data.description: UNITED NATIONS - The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a new resolution calling for an end to the US embargo against Cuba, although support for the communist-ruled island fell to its lowest level in three decades.

data.title: Nurses oppose govt volunteer plans
data.description: The Nurses Association of Thailand has opposed the government's Community Nursing Volunteer initiative, urging authorities to review the policy and promote oversight to protect patient safety and healthcare standards.

data.title: Mister Donut & After You Partner Again After Selling 2 Million Donuts
data.description: Mister Donut, operated by Central Restaurants Group Co., Ltd. (CRG), is continuing its brand collaboration strategy by partnering with After You for “Mister Donut x After You Season 2”. Following the success of their first collaboration, which sold nearly 2 million donuts and generated strong buzz across social media, the two brands are introducing five new creations under the “Japanese Autumn” concept. Inspired by Japan’s autumn season, the collection combines distinctive flavours and textures, highlighted by a specially developed mochi donut recipe created exclusively for this campaign. The collaboration aims to introduce innovative dessert experiences, attract new consumer segments, and strengthen the brands’ market presence.

data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Wednesday criticised media reports linking major corporations, including Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc, to the government's household solar rooftop scheme, rejecting claims that the project was designed to favour large businesses.

data.title: PP backs groups opposing fund law changes
data.description: Opposition People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut said he shared the concerns of civil society groups opposing amendments to four laws that would change the funding arrangements for public bodies.

data.title: Aluminium in river 'poses low risk' to environment
data.description: The Department of Pollution Control says aluminium detected in the Prachin Buri River is unlikely to pose a significant risk to health or the environment, as the water's pH level may cause the metal to settle in river sediments.

data.title: Tax revenue shake-up draws fire
